description: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs,” illustrates the distribution of responses regarding whether individuals felt “Deceived” during conversations across four distinct contexts: Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, Academic Funding, and Journalism. The x-axis represents the “Number of Conversations,” ranging from 0 to 60 in increments of 10, while the y-axis lists the four categories. Each category is represented by three adjacent horizontal bars, color-coded according to the legend: red for “Yes” (deceived), yellow for “Partially,” and green for “No.” In “Academic Collaboration,” approximately 36 conversations resulted in “Yes,” 27 in “Partially,” and 7 in “No.” For “Recruitment,” “Yes” responses total around 38, “Partially” about 24, and “No” roughly 6. “Academic Funding” shows the highest “Yes” count at approximately 65, with “Partially” at about 4 and “No” at 3. In “Journalism,” “Yes” responses are around 15, “Partially” reach nearly 48, and “No” are about 6. The chart visually emphasizes that deception perception varies significantly by context, with “Academic Funding” having the highest rate of full deception and “Journalism” the highest rate of partial deception.
